StatusLIVE EXECUTIVE DASHBOARD
PurposeFounder-level command board for customer, supplier, product, market, and cash-dependency concentration so growth quality does not become fragile.
Source ruleUpdate customer account review, supplier performance review, trade profitability review, revenue forecast, cash forecast, capital allocation, sales pipeline, and executive risk register first, then refresh this review.
Founder useDecide where concentration is acceptable strategic focus, where it has become hidden fragility, and what proof is required before more capital, release, or founder attention concentrates in the same place.
Protection ruleThis dashboard governs concentration posture only; approved templates, brand assets, and source-record protections stay unchanged.

Concentration Control PostureLink

Control lensCurrent postureFounder readRequired response
Customer concentrationAtlantic Foods and HarborFresh still carry too much near-term weight.Concentrated growth can be useful, but it becomes fragile when cash timing and release logic depend on the same accounts.Tie top-account growth to cash, credit, trust, and diversification proof.
Product concentrationGarlic remains the dominant gross-profit family.Product focus is producing margin, but disruption would hit cash, supply, and customer delivery at once.Advance adjacent SKU pipeline and backup sourcing before garlic comfort becomes false resilience.
Supplier concentrationGolden Harvest remains the most important supplier cluster.Supplier performance is strong enough to use, not strong enough to overdepend on.Keep backup-source proof live and route delays into supply resilience and risk review.
Cash concentrationAtlantic Foods remains too important to short-term liquidity timing.Revenue concentration is manageable only if cash exposure does not move with it.Treat cash timing dependence as a release and capital-allocation constraint.
Founder attention concentrationThe same account family keeps touching pricing, credit, claims, trust, and exceptions.Concentration also consumes executive bandwidth, not only revenue share.Route stacked issues through matter control, exception governance, and owner accountability.

Concentration Exposure BandsLink

Exposure bandConditionFounder postureRequired control action
Strategic focusConcentration is intentional, profitable, cash-clean, and supported by backup paths.Permit growth while monitoring.Keep source records current and protect margins.
Controlled watchConcentration is useful but still depends on one customer, supplier, region, or product family.Allow only with dated mitigation proof.Link to pipeline, supply resilience, cash, and risk controls.
Capital constraintConcentration could absorb scarce cash, release capacity, credit, or founder attention.Do not widen exposure casually.Require capital allocation and cash forecast support before expansion.
Fragility warningConcentration creates synchronized downside across cash, revenue, supply, or trust.Treat as executive risk.Route to risk register, scenario response, and plan variance.
Stop-expansionConcentrated exposure lacks proof, owner, fallback, or recovery path.Pause further reliance.Hold commitments until diversification or containment evidence improves.

Diversification Proof StandardLink

Diversification proofMinimum evidenceWeak substitute to rejectFounder read
Customer diversificationQualified account, next dated buyer action, credit posture, and forecast band impact.Lead name without stage movement.New accounts matter only when they reduce top-account dependence.
Supplier diversificationBackup capacity proof, quality evidence, compliance readiness, and scenario path.Verbal supplier comfort.Backup supply is real only when it can absorb pressure.
Product diversificationNon-garlic pipeline, pricing posture, margin model, and shipment feasibility.Broad SKU interest without economics.Product mix should improve resilience, not dilute focus.
Market diversificationNon-Florida buyer path, logistics fit, account owner, and next review date.Geographic aspiration without active buyer movement.Regional resilience requires concrete customer motion.
Cash diversificationReceivable cadence, collections evidence, release discipline, and cash forecast impact.Confidence that payment timing will normalize.Cash quality is the hardest concentration proof.

Escalation and Stop RulesLink

RuleConditionRequired escalationFounder action
Cash concentration stopTop-account cash dependence rises or collection proof weakens while exposure remains high.Route to cash forecast, collections control, credit release, and capital allocation.Hold release expansion until cash proof improves.
Product concentration stopGarlic margin exposure rises without backup source or adjacent SKU proof.Route to supply resilience, trade profitability, and risk register.Cap promise aggression until fallback proof is current.
Customer exception stackingOne account requires pricing, release, trust, remedy, or CAPA exceptions in the same cycle.Route to exception governance and matter control.Consolidate exception map before new approvals.
Pipeline proof failureDiversification remains activity-only without qualified stage movement.Route to sales pipeline and strategic initiatives.Reject diversification credit until buyer proof exists.
Capital overconcentrationConcentrated exposure asks for more cash, release, or capacity support without mitigation.Route to capital allocation and founder decisions.Reallocate or pause until exposure band improves.
